title: Recurrent Pregnancy Loss, Cervical Incompetence and MTP

units.title: Abortion Epidemiology & Chromosomal Etiology
units.guide: Spontaneous abortion is defined as the loss of pregnancy prior to viability (<20 weeks or <500 g; legal viability in India is historically 28 weeks). Approximately 50-60% of first-trimester miscarriages result from chromosomal anomalies: autosomal trisomies are the most common category (Trisomy 16 is the most common and universally lethal; Trisomy 21 is the most viable), while Monosomy X (45,X0 / Turner syndrome) is the single most common individual chromosomal defect.

units.title: Recurrent Pregnancy Loss: Etiology & Diagnostic Workup
units.guide: Recurrent Pregnancy Loss (RPL) is defined as two or more consecutive clinical pregnancy losses. Antiphospholipid syndrome is the leading treatable autoimmune etiology, while endocrine causes include uncontrolled hypothyroidism and PCOS; congenital uterine anomalies (septate uterus having the highest miscarriage rate) and parental balanced reciprocal or Robertsonian translocations (requiring parental karyotyping) represent structural causes.

units.title: Cervical Incompetence: Sonography & Management Indications
units.guide: Cervical incompetence is characterized by painless cervical dilation during the second trimester leading to prolapse and rupture of membranes. Transvaginal ultrasound confirms the diagnosis when cervical length is <=25 mm or internal os funneling progresses through T, Y, V, and U shapes; management includes prophylactic vaginal progesterone (from 16 to 36 weeks) and cervical cerclage placed between 12 and 14 weeks.

units.title: Cervical Cerclage: Shirodkar, McDonald & Rescue Techniques
units.guide: The two primary transvaginal cerclage procedures are Shirodkar (submucosal tape placed at internal os following bladder reflection) and McDonald (purse-string non-absorbable suture placed in the portio vaginalis without bladder dissection); emergency/rescue cerclage (or Wurm cross-mattress suture) is attempted when the cervix is dilated <4 cm with unruptured membranes. Sutures are removed electively at 37 weeks.

units.title: Antiphospholipid Syndrome: Sapporo Criteria & Anticoagulation
units.guide: Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (APS) is diagnosed by modified Sapporo/Sydney criteria requiring at least one clinical criterion (vascular thrombosis or adverse pregnancy loss) and one persistent laboratory criterion (Lupus Anticoagulant, Anticardiolipin IgG/IgM, or Anti-beta2-glycoprotein I IgG/IgM verified 12 weeks apart). Management in pregnancy consists of low-dose aspirin (75-150 mg) plus prophylactic LMWH (heparin) initiated upon positive urine pregnancy test.

units.title: Clinical Varieties: Threatened, Inevitable, Incomplete & Missed
units.guide: Spontaneous abortions are classified by clinical presentation: Threatened (cervix closed, viable fetus, brown spotting/mild cramping; managed conservatively), Inevitable (cervix open, active bleeding, cramps; irreversible), Incomplete (cervix open with partial expulsion of products of conception, causing hemorrhage), Complete (cervix closed, all products expelled), and Missed (cervix closed, empty sac >=25 mm MSD or embryo CRL >=7 mm without cardiac activity).

units.title: Septic Abortion & MTP Act (2021 Amendments)
units.guide: Septic abortion is an abortion complicated by intrauterine infection presenting with purulent discharge, pelvic pain, high fever, and potentially toxic shock; managed with broad-spectrum parenteral antibiotics and early evacuation. Under India's MTP Amendment Act 2021, abortion is permitted up to 20 weeks with 1 RMP opinion, up to 24 weeks with 2 RMPs for vulnerable categories (rape, minors, disability), and without gestational age limit for severe fetal anomalies approved by a State Medical Board.

units.title: Medical & Surgical Abortion Techniques: Protocols & Complications
units.guide: First-trimester medical abortion up to 9 weeks (63 days) uses oral Mifepristone 200 mg followed 24-48 hours later by Misoprostol 800 mcg. Surgical termination uses Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA syringe, 600 mmHg negative pressure) or Suction & Evacuation (Karman cannula size equal to gestational weeks) under paracervical block; if uterine perforation occurs with a suction cannula, the cannula is held in place without withdrawal while stabilizing the patient and evaluating by laparoscopy/laparotomy.

questions.q: What is the global definition of spontaneous abortion according to the WHO and CDC?
opts: Involuntary termination of pregnancy before 20 completed weeks of gestation or expulsion of an embryo/fetus weighing less than 500 grams
Expulsion of pregnancy before 28 weeks only
Termination of pregnancy before 32 weeks of gestation
Fetal demise occurring exclusively during the first 6 weeks of gestation
questions.exp: Spontaneous abortion is defined as pregnancy loss occurring before 20 weeks of gestation or fetal weight < 500 g. (Book p418)

questions.q: What is the single most common cause of first-trimester spontaneous pregnancy loss?
opts: Fetal chromosomal abnormalities / genetic aneuploidies (accounting for 50% to 60% of cases)
questions.exp: Chromosomal anomalies (predominantly numerical aneuploidies) account for over 50-60% of all spontaneous first-trimester abortions. (Book p418)

questions.q: Among chromosomal aneuploidies causing spontaneous first-trimester abortion, what is the single MOST FREQUENT and most lethal autosomal trisomy?
opts: Trisomy 16 (never survives to term; accounts for ~30% of all trisomic abortions)
questions.exp: Trisomy 16 is the most common and universally lethal trisomy found in abortuses; it never results in a live birth. (Book p419)

questions.q: What is the single MOST COMMON individual chromosomal abnormality identified in early spontaneous abortuses overall?
questions.exp: Monosomy X (45,X0) is the most common single specific chromosomal karyotype error seen in spontaneous abortions (~20% of aneuploid losses). (Book p419)

questions.q: Which autosomal trisomy is the MOST VIABLE, yet most frequently terminates in spontaneous abortion during pregnancy?
questions.exp: Trisomy 21 is the most viable autosomal trisomy at birth, but the majority (~75-80%) of Trisomy 21 conceptuses abort spontaneously in utero. (Book p419)

questions.q: How is Recurrent Pregnancy Loss (RPL) defined clinically by the European Society of Human Reproduction and Embryology (ESHRE) and ASRM?
opts: The consecutive loss of two or more clinical pregnancies
questions.exp: RPL is defined as two or more consecutive pregnancy losses, justifying initiation of a diagnostic evaluation. (Book p419)

questions.q: What is the most common treatable autoimmune cause of recurrent pregnancy loss?
questions.exp: APLA is the single most common and treatable acquired thrombophilic/autoimmune cause of recurrent pregnancy loss. (Book p419)

questions.q: Which congenital uterine structural malformation carries the HIGHEST incidence of spontaneous pregnancy loss?
opts: Septate uterus (due to poor avascular fibroelastic septum implantation)
questions.exp: A uterine septum has deficient vascularity and endometrial development; implantation onto the septum carries a >65% miscarriage rate. (Book p419)

questions.q: What is the most common parental chromosomal abnormality discovered upon karyotyping couples with recurrent pregnancy loss?
questions.exp: Parental balanced reciprocal translocations occur in 2-5% of RPL couples, producing unbalanced gametes upon meiotic segregation. (Book p420)

questions.q: Which routine test is explicitly NOT RECOMMENDED in the diagnostic evaluation of recurrent pregnancy loss?
opts: Routine TORCH serology screening (because acute TORCH infections cause sporadic, not recurrent miscarriages)
Pelvic transvaginal ultrasound for Mullerian anomalies
questions.exp: TORCH infections do not cause recurrent pregnancy loss; screening for TORCH in recurrent abortion is obsolete and unjustified. (Book p420)

questions.q: What classic obstetric history strongly points toward the diagnosis of cervical incompetence (cervical insufficiency)?
opts: Recurrent, painless second-trimester miscarriages characterized by rapid expulsion of a live, morphologically normal fetus without prior uterine contractions
Severe painful first-trimester cramps with passage of heavy clots
Painless third-trimester bright red vaginal bleeding
questions.exp: Cervical incompetence typically presents as painless cervical dilation in the 2nd trimester, leading to membrane prolapse and rapid fetal expulsion. (Book p420)

questions.q: What cervical length on transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) during the second trimester (16-24 weeks) establishes the diagnosis of a short cervix?
questions.exp: A TVS cervical length <= 25 mm before 24 weeks represents the 10th percentile and defines a short cervix at high risk for preterm loss. (Book p420)

questions.q: What is the correct sequential mnemonic for the progressive stages of internal cervical os funneling seen on ultrasound in cervical insufficiency?
opts: T -> Y -> V -> U ('Trust Your Vaginal Ultrasound')
questions.exp: Mnemonic 'TYVU' represents progressive endocervical effacement: T (normal closed T-shape), Y (early funneling), V (advanced), U (hourglass prolapse). (Book p420)

questions.q: When is a history-indicated cervical cerclage recommended?
opts: In a woman with a history of >= 2 to 3 second-trimester painless losses or preterm deliveries, placed electively at 12 to 14 weeks regardless of cervical length
Only when cervix is 5 cm dilated in labor
In all primigravid women with twins
questions.exp: History-indicated cerclage is placed electively at 12-14 weeks for women with classical history of >= 2-3 painless 2nd-trimester deliveries. (Book p420)

questions.q: What medical therapy is proven to prevent preterm birth in an asymptomatic singleton pregnancy found to have a short cervical length (<=25 mm) on TVS at 18-24 weeks?
opts: Daily vaginal natural micronized progesterone (200 mg nightly) until 36 completed weeks
Complete strict supine bed rest for 5 months
questions.exp: Vaginal progesterone reduces preterm delivery by ~40-50% in asymptomatic women with a TVS-detected short cervix <= 25 mm. (Book p421)

questions.q: What is the key surgical difference between the McDonald cerclage and the Shirodkar cerclage?
opts: McDonald is a simple purse-string suture placed in the portio vaginalis without bladder dissection, whereas Shirodkar requires anterior bladder reflection to place tape at the level of the internal os
McDonald requires a laparotomy, while Shirodkar is vaginal
McDonald uses metal clips, while Shirodkar uses silk
questions.exp: McDonald is simpler without mucosal dissection; Shirodkar reflects the bladder anteriorly to place Mersilene tape right at the internal os. (Book p421)

questions.q: What is the primary suture material commonly used for Shirodkar cervical cerclage?
opts: Mersilene tape (5 mm braided polyester non-absorbable tape)
questions.exp: Mersilene tape (5 mm broad polyester tape) provides robust mechanical strength and prevents tissue cutting around the internal cervical os. (Book p422)

questions.q: At what gestational age is an elective transvaginal cervical cerclage suture typically REMOVED?
opts: At 36 to 37 completed weeks of gestation (or earlier if spontaneous active labor or rupture of membranes supervenes)
During the postpartum period after delivery
questions.exp: Vaginal cerclage is removed at 36-37 weeks to prevent cervical dystocia and severe laceration when spontaneous labor begins. (Book p422)

questions.q: What is the Wurm cerclage technique, used primarily in emergency or rescue cerclage settings?
opts: Placement of two criss-crossing mattress sutures through the cervix in anteroposterior and transverse directions forming a '+' or 'X' shape
A single absorbable suture at the external os
A permanent metal band around the uterine fundus
questions.exp: Wurm cerclage uses two mattress sutures (one AP, one transverse) to close a dilated cervix when purse-string placement is technically difficult. (Book p422)

questions.q: Which of the following is an ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION to performing a cervical cerclage?
opts: Active intrauterine infection / chorioamnionitis, or ruptured fetal membranes (PPROM)
History of one prior spontaneous abortion
questions.exp: Chorioamnionitis, active uterine bleeding, ruptured membranes, active preterm labor, and lethal fetal anomalies are absolute contraindications. (Book p423)

questions.q: Which three antiphospholipid antibodies are included in the laboratory criteria for diagnosing Antiphospholipid Antibody Syndrome (APLA)?
opts: Lupus Anticoagulant (LA), Anti-cardiolipin antibodies (IgG/IgM), and Anti-beta2-glycoprotein I antibodies (IgG/IgM)
questions.exp: APLA laboratory criteria require Lupus Anticoagulant, Anticardiolipin (IgG/IgM), or Anti-beta2-glycoprotein I (IgG/IgM) verified on >= 2 occasions 12 weeks apart. (Book p424)

questions.q: In the modified Sapporo / Sydney criteria for APLA, which obstetric history fulfills the clinical criteria?
opts: >= 3 consecutive spontaneous abortions before 10 weeks, OR >= 1 unexplained fetal death at >= 10 weeks, OR >= 1 preterm delivery before 34 weeks due to severe pre-eclampsia/placental insufficiency
questions.exp: Clinical criteria: >=3 consecutive losses <10w, >=1 loss >=10w with normal morphology, or >=1 preterm birth <34w d/t severe pre-eclampsia/UPI. (Book p424)

questions.q: What paradoxical coagulation abnormality is seen in patients with Lupus Anticoagulant on routine coagulation screening in the laboratory?
opts: Isolated prolongation of Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT) in vitro, despite causing in vivo hypercoagulability and thrombosis
Profoundly shortened aPTT with prolonged PT
Isolated reduction in platelet count without coagulation changes
questions.exp: Lupus anticoagulant binds phospholipids in vitro, artificially delaying coagulation and prolonging aPTT, but promotes thrombosis in vivo. (Book p424)

questions.q: What is the evidence-based medical treatment of choice for pregnant women with APLA and recurrent pregnancy loss?
opts: Low-dose Aspirin (75-150 mg daily) PLUS prophylactic Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin (LMWH), initiated as soon as pregnancy is confirmed
questions.exp: Combination of low-dose aspirin and prophylactic LMWH (started at positive pregnancy test) raises live birth rates to >70-80% in APLA. (Book p425)

questions.q: In a non-pregnant patient with Antiphospholipid Syndrome and a history of deep vein thrombosis, what is the anticoagulant drug of choice for long-term secondary prevention?
questions.exp: Warfarin (INR 2.0-3.0) is the definitive long-term oral anticoagulant for secondary thrombosis prevention in non-pregnant APS patients. (Book p425)

questions.q: A pregnant woman at 8 weeks presents with mild vaginal spotting and lower backache. Examination reveals a closed internal os, uterine size corresponding to gestational age, and ultrasound demonstrates a viable intrauterine fetus with cardiac activity. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Threatened abortion features vaginal spotting/mild cramping with a closed internal cervical os and documented viable cardiac activity. (Book p425)

questions.q: What key clinical finding differentiates an INEVITABLE abortion from a THREATENED abortion?
opts: Internal cervical os is dilated / open in inevitable abortion, whereas it remains tightly closed in threatened abortion
Cardiac activity is always present in inevitable abortion
Uterine size is twice the gestational age in inevitable abortion
Threatened abortion is accompanied by foul purulent discharge
questions.exp: Dilation of the internal cervical os indicates irreversible progression to inevitable abortion, whereas the os is closed in threatened abortion. (Book p425)

questions.q: A woman presents with severe vaginal hemorrhage and lower abdominal cramps. On speculum examination, the internal cervical os is open with placental tissue protruding through the canal. Uterine size is smaller than the period of amenorrhea. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Incomplete abortion features partial expulsion of products of conception with cervical os open, active bleeding, and smaller-than-dates uterus. (Book p425)

questions.q: What ultrasound criteria definitively establish the diagnosis of early pregnancy failure (missed abortion / non-viable embryo)?
opts: Crown-Rump Length (CRL) >= 7 mm without cardiac activity, OR Mean Sac Diameter (MSD) >= 25 mm without an embryo
Absence of fetal heart on transabdominal scan at 4 weeks
questions.exp: Established criteria for non-viable pregnancy: CRL >= 7 mm with no heartbeat, or mean gestational sac diameter >= 25 mm with no embryo. (Book p426)

questions.q: In a patient presenting with spontaneous abortion who suddenly develops hypovolemic shock, what are the two most common underlying causes in order of frequency?
opts: Septic abortion followed by Incomplete abortion (causing torrential hemorrhage or endotoxemia)
Missed abortion followed by threatened abortion
Complete abortion followed by blighted ovum
questions.exp: Shock complicating abortion is most commonly due to septic abortion (distributive/septic shock) followed closely by incomplete abortion (hemorrhagic shock). (Book p426)

questions.q: What is the clinical definition and staging of Grade 3 septic abortion?
opts: Infection that has spread beyond the pelvis to produce generalized peritonitis, septic shock, or acute renal failure
Infection confined exclusively to the endometrial cavity (Grade 1)
Infection extending into parametrium and adnexa (Grade 2)
questions.exp: Grade 1 is limited to the uterus, Grade 2 extends to adnexa/broad ligament, and Grade 3 involves peritonitis, pelvic abscess, septic shock, or renal failure. (Book p426)

questions.q: Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act 2021 in India, what is the gestational limit up to which ONE Registered Medical Practitioner (RMP) can approve an MTP?
questions.exp: Under the 2021 amendments, termination up to 20 weeks requires the opinion of only one RMP (increased from the previous 12-week limit). (Book p427)

questions.q: Under the MTP Amendment Act 2021, for vulnerable categories of women (e.g., rape survivors, incest victims, minors, women with physical disability), up to what gestational age is pregnancy termination allowed with the opinion of TWO RMPs?
questions.exp: For special categories (rape survivors, minors, change of marital status during pregnancy), the upper limit is extended to 24 weeks with 2 RMPs. (Book p427)

questions.q: If a severe substantial congenital fetal abnormality is diagnosed, what is the gestational upper age limit for medical termination under the MTP Amendment Act 2021?
opts: No upper gestational age limit applies, provided the termination is approved by a four-member State Medical Board
questions.exp: The 24-week cap does not apply to cases of substantial fetal abnormalities diagnosed by the four-member State Medical Board. (Book p427)

questions.q: Whose legal consent is mandatory for performing a Medical Termination of Pregnancy on a woman who is 19 years old and mentally sound?
opts: Consent of the woman herself alone; husband or parental consent is NOT legally required
Consent of her husband or partner
Consent of both her parents and in-laws
questions.exp: Under the MTP Act, any adult woman (>= 18 years) can provide valid autonomous consent; spousal or family consent is not required by law. (Book p427)

questions.q: What is the approved regimen for first-trimester Medical Abortion on an outpatient basis up to 9 weeks (63 days) of gestation?
opts: Day 1: Tab Mifepristone 200 mg orally; Day 3: Tab Misoprostol 800 mcg (buccal, sublingual, or vaginal); Day 14-15: Clinical/USG follow-up
Misoprostol 200 mcg single oral dose without mifepristone
questions.exp: Mifepristone 200 mg PO followed 24-48h later by misoprostol 800 mcg produces >95% complete abortion rate up to 63 days of gestation. (Book p428)

questions.q: What is the pharmacological mechanism of action of Mifepristone (RU-486)?
opts: Potent synthetic competitive progesterone receptor antagonist, causing decidual necrosis, blastocyst detachment, and cervical softening
Synthetic prostaglandin E1 analog stimulating myometrial contractions
questions.exp: Mifepristone competitively blocks intracellular progesterone receptors, triggering decidual breakdown, trophoblast detachment, and sensitization to prostaglandins. (Book p428)

questions.q: During Suction & Evacuation using a Karman cannula, what negative suction pressure is generated, and what is the rule of thumb for selecting cannula size?
opts: Negative pressure >= 600 mmHg; Cannula diameter in millimeters roughly equals the period of gestation in completed weeks
Negative pressure of 100 mmHg; cannula size 2 mm for all gestations
Positive pressure of 300 mmHg; cannula size 18 mm
questions.exp: Suction pressure is maintained at >= 600 mmHg; Karman cannula number corresponds to its outer diameter in mm and approximates gestational weeks. (Book p430)

questions.q: Where is local anesthetic injected during a paracervical block for first-trimester surgical abortion, and which locations are avoided to protect the uterine arteries?
opts: Injected at 4 and 8 o'clock (or 2, 4, 8, 10 o'clock) positions; the 3 and 9 o'clock positions are avoided to prevent inadvertent intravascular uterine artery injection
Injected directly into the 3 and 9 o'clock vascular pedicles
Injected solely into the anterior cervical lip at 12 o'clock
Injected into the posterior vaginal fornix at 6 o'clock
questions.exp: Injections are placed at 4 and 8 (or 2, 4, 8, 10) o'clock; the 3 and 9 o'clock lateral positions are avoided to prevent injecting into descending cervical vessels. (Book p430)

questions.q: During Suction & Evacuation, the surgeon notes a sudden loss of resistance and the Karman cannula passes deeper than expected. What is the immediate correct management?
opts: Stop the procedure immediately, leave the cannula in place without moving it, check vital signs, and call for senior surgical assistance
Vigorously rotate the cannula to complete suctioning
Administer high-dose oxytocin and withdraw the cannula quickly
Discharge the patient with oral antibiotics
questions.exp: If perforation is suspected with a suction cannula, leaving it still prevents dragging bowel loops or mesentery through the uterine defect. (Book p431)
